AgentIdentity.description:
Who a detected agent is.

Open rather than an enum of the tools Rozi happens to know: `id` and `label` both come from the
[`AgentDefinition`](crate::agent_detection::AgentDefinition) that matched, and a definition
declared in `config.toml` or shipped by an extension produces one of these exactly as a built-in
does. Nothing downstream may branch on a known set of ids - the sidebar renders `label`.

id.description: Stable definition id, such as `claude` or `git-tools.mycoolagent`.

label.description: Display name, as the definition declared it.

unless_quiet.description:
Set when the reporter cannot know a later report will follow, such as a hook that another
hook can stop the turn after. Every other report outranks the screen.

AgentLocationSpec.description: Where an agent runs, as `agents-overview` reports it and `agent-go` takes it back.

host.description: The connected host, spelled the way `--remote` takes it. Absent for this machine.

row.description: The published row, for a program running several agents in one pane.

AgentRecord.description:
What the session server tracks about one agent reference beyond the reference itself.

`completions` counts the runs this incarnation has finished: each time it was working and then
idle or done, with any wait for approval in between. The server counts every transition it
makes, so a client comparing two values learns that a run ended even when it never saw the agent
working - a monitor polling between the two, or a client that was detached at the time. A new
incarnation starts again from zero, which is why the count is only meaningful beside the
reference it belongs to.

AgentRef.description: Exact identity of one semantic agent or published activity.

slot.description: The published agent row this reference names, or `None` for the pane's own agent.

AgentResponsePayload.description: Content supplied by an integration, separate from lifecycle metadata.

oneOf.description: The run failed. It ended, but not with a result worth reading as done.

AgentSummary.description: One agent's state, as reported by the session server that owns it.

agent.description:
Agent id: the detected or reported definition (`claude`, `codex`), or for an agent publisher
in a pane with neither, the row's own id.

changed_at.description: Unix milliseconds when this pane's semantic agent state last changed.

completions.description: Runs this agent has finished. See [`super::AgentRecord::completions`].

label.description:
The agent's display name (`Claude Code`). Several agents of one pane share it; [`Self::task`]
is what tells them apart.

reason.description: Why the agent is in its state, as it said (`Permission required`).

reference.description:
Which agent this is: its pane, that pane's spawn generation, the published row for a pane
running several agents, and the incarnation of the occupant. Everything identifying is
here, so a respawned pane, a relaunched agent, or a row that left and came back each read as
a different agent rather than as the old one changing state.

screen_title.description:
What a pane's own agent calls its work in its terminal title, when that says more than its
name or its directory: what names a run with no [`Self::task`]. `None` for a published row,
whose title is its task. See [`super::agent_title::screen_title`].

task.description: What the agent works on, when it named its work. See [`super::AgentRuntime::task`].

oneOf.description: A prompted turn finished or needs intervention.

live_catch_up_bytes.description: Post-baseline output/control retained in memory or queued behind replay.

queued_bytes.description: Encoded baseline replay currently waiting in socket outboxes.

replay_bytes_total.description: Replay payload exported across this server process's lifetime.

AttachmentOperation.description: One acknowledged step of a bounded attachment upload.

oneOf.description: A step from a newer peer this build does not know. Never sent.

BranchCopy.description: Which copy of a branch an outcome is about.

remote.description: The remote's name, unknown when the branch has no usable upstream.

BranchDeletion.description: Which copies of a removed checkout's branch to delete. Both off keeps the branch.

local.description: The local branch, if fully merged.

remote.description: The branch on the remote it tracks, if its fetched tip is merged into the primary checkout.

BranchOutcome.description: What happened to one copy of a removed checkout's branch.

oneOf.description: Git or a guard here kept the branch; `reason` says why.

Capabilities.description:
An open set of capability names. Unknown ones deserialize and are dropped during negotiation,
so a future peer offering more than this build knows is downgraded rather than refused.

CaptureRender.description: What form `capture-pane` returns a pane in, and `capture-ui` the whole client.

oneOf.description: Plain text, the only form that can include scrollback.

The visible grid as text with SGR color and style sequences: no cursor movement or screen
clearing, every row at the full width.

The visible grid as a PNG image, in the theme's colors, with the images a program displayed
drawn over their cells.

The visible grid as a [`SpanFrame`]: each row's styled runs, the cursor, and the images a
program displayed, as JSON.

anyOf.description: Trailing line count from the retained scrollback + live grid.

CaptureScrollback.description: How many scrollback lines `capture-pane` should include when not using the visible grid.

CaptureScrollbackNamed.description:
Named `capture-pane` scrollback modes. Serde maps these to kebab-case strings so
validation lives in the type instead of string compares at each call site.

CellRect.description:
A rectangle in terminal cells. The origin can be negative or lie past the canvas: a Scrollable
strip is wider than the canvas it scrolls across, and a follower letterboxes a larger canonical
canvas into a smaller screen.

parked.description:
True while this client holds the session open in the background rather than displaying it.
A parked client is still attached — its screens stay live and switching back is instant —
but it is not an occupant: it never holds the layout-control lease and is skipped when the
lease has to move, so a background connection cannot push the next client into follower
mode. Broadcast in the roster so the clients view can say which clients are only parked.

requesting_control.description:
True while this client has an outstanding request for the layout-control lease that the
controller has not yet granted or declined. Broadcast in the roster so every client can badge
the pending request; cleared when control moves to it or the controller declines.

ClientLayoutView.description: What one UI is looking at. Nothing here is shared with other clients.

committed.description:
False while this UI has layout changes the server has not yet accepted, so `revision` does
not describe them. Always true for a follower.

controller.description: Whether this UI holds the session's layout-control lease.

expected_server_nonce.description:
One-time identity proof for a server this client just spawned. Ordinary attaches omit
it; when present, a same-name server with a different startup nonce must reject attach.

handoff_token.description:
Claim the client slot a departing client reserved with
[`ClientMessage::PrepareHandoff`]: its layout-control lease and parked state pass to this
connection. A token the server does not hold - expired, spent, or never issued - is
ignored and the attach proceeds as an ordinary one. Sent only to a server that
negotiated [`super::Capability::ClientHandoff`].

shares_filesystem.description:
Whether this client can open paths the session's children write.

A child may hand the terminal a frame by naming a file instead of pasting megabytes of
pixels into the byte stream, but only a client on the server's own machine can go and
read it. Attaching over SSH says so here, and the server stops offering that route.
Absent on a peer that predates the field, where refusing is the safe reading.

oneOf.description:
Record the provenance that supplied this session's initial panes. Sent only after the seed
requests have been queued successfully.

Headless control: run one [`crate::control::ControlCommand`] against this session and
answer with its [`crate::control::ControlResponse`].

Like [`Self::Query`] and unlike [`Self::Attach`], the connection is never registered as a
client: no client id, no roster entry, no layout lease, no replay seeding, and the server
closes it once the reply has flushed. That is the whole point — a script inspecting or
driving a detached session must not make the session look occupied, and must not pay for a
full attach to type one line into a pane.

Only the subset of commands a session server can answer on its own is accepted; the rest
belong to a UI process and are refused by name (see
[`crate::session::server::session_control_unsupported`]).

Picker probe: report session status without registering the connection as a client and
without any replay seeding. Cheap enough to run against many sockets concurrently.

cell_width.description:
Host cell size in pixels, so the PTY reports pixel dimensions a child that draws
images can use. Zero (the pre-17 default) leaves the PTY's own default in place.

command_shell.description:
Resolved command-runner argv (non-empty; program then fixed args), resolved
client-side via `platform::command::resolve_command_shell`. Only used for
[`PaneLaunch::Shell`](crate::pane::launch::PaneLaunch::Shell).

local.description:
Owner-scoped transient pane. Local panes may reuse another client's pane id, are
operable by their owner without the layout lease, and die with that client.

palette.description:
Terminal color palette seeded onto the server screen *before* the PTY spawns, so the
child's startup OSC 4/10/11 color queries are answered with the theme palette rather
than the screen default. Sending it out-of-band via `SetPalette` races the child's
query, so it must ride along with the spawn request.

placement.description: Required for shared panes; forbidden for owner-local panes.

shell.description:
Resolved interactive-shell argv (non-empty; program then fixed args), resolved
client-side via `platform::command::resolve_interactive_shell` against the live
config. Used verbatim when `launch` is `None`; also used to `exec` into after a shell
command or direct process completes when `keep_open` is set (see [`ServerPane`] docs).

cell_height.description: Host cell height in pixels. See `cell_width`.

cell_width.description:
Host cell width in pixels, from the controller. Zero (the pre-17 default) means the
client did not report one; the server keeps whatever the PTY already had.

local.description: Address the owner-local namespace when true; the shared session namespace when false.

oneOf.description:
Run one session-owned [`crate::control::ControlCommand`] on behalf of this attached
client, answered by [`ServerMessage::AttachedControlResult`] with the same `request_id`.

The attached counterpart of [`Self::SessionControl`]: the connection stays open and the
answer may arrive after unrelated traffic, so the client matches it by `request_id`. Only
the commands a UI has no way to serve itself are accepted (see
[`crate::session::server::attached_control_refusal`]).

The caller of an [`Self::AttachedControl`] has gone, so stop the action call it started. The
call still answers `request_id`.

Replace one publisher's rows in the pane, leaving every other publisher's alone. An empty
list withdraws them; once no agent publisher has rows, the pane falls back to screen
detection.

Re-read the agent definitions this session detects with.

Carries no payload: the server loads its own config, which is the same file the client
resolved (`--config` propagates to `--server`) and, over `--remote`, is correctly the
*remote* host's - where the processes being detected actually run. Accepted only from the
controller, since `detected_agent` is one shared answer for every attached client rather
than a per-client view. Sent after a config reload; a session that never reloads gets its
definitions from the same load at startup.
Reload the server's spawn policy and capacity for future panes.
Controller-only: re-read the host config for its agent sleep policy. No client payload.

Commit a new shared layout. Accepted only from the controller and only when `base_rev`
equals the server's current revision; otherwise the server replies [`ServerMessage::LayoutRejected`].

live.description:
Committed in the middle of a pointer gesture (a split drag, a mouse resize, or a floating
pane move). Relayed on [`ServerMessage::LayoutCommitted`] so followers apply it directly.

oneOf.description:
Controller-only: a tiled pane is lifted out of the tiling and is currently at `rect`.

Transient presence state, relayed rather than recorded: it carries no revision, is never
merged into the shared layout, and the server keeps none of it. Sent continuously for the
length of the gesture, so a follower can lift the same pane instead of watching the tiles
behind it reflow around a pane that never moved.

rect.description: Fractions of the controller's canonical canvas, matching `SharedPane::rect`.

oneOf.description:
Controller-only: the tiled drag is over.

The controller commits the resulting layout *before* sending this, and both ride the same
ordered stream, so every follower has applied the authoritative tree by the time it stops
lifting the pane. Reversing the two would drop the pane back into its old slot for a frame.

Request the layout-control lease. The server grants immediately when there is no controller
or takeover is enabled; otherwise it flags this client as requesting and notifies the
controller (see [`ServerMessage::ControlRequested`]).

Controller-only: allow or forbid writable followers from taking the lease immediately when
they send [`ClientMessage::RequestControl`].

Declare whether this client is parked: still attached, with its screens kept live, but not
displaying or driving the session. Parking releases the layout-control lease if this client
held it and excludes it from promotion, so a client keeping several sessions open in the
background does not make each of them look occupied to the next client that attaches.
Unparking asks for the lease back, which the server auto-grants when nobody holds it.
Controller-only: grant the lease to `to`, which also clears `to`'s pending request.

Controller-only: reject `to`'s pending control request, clearing its flag and notifying it
(see [`ServerMessage::ControlDeclined`]).

Controller-only: remove `target` from the session. The server sends the
target an [`ServerMessage::Error`] carrying [`super::constants::EVICTED_ERROR_CODE`] and then closes its
connection; the session itself and every other client keep running.

Reserve this client's slot for the process that replaces it, such as the same client
relaunched on a newer build. The server answers [`ServerMessage::HandoffPrepared`] with a
one-time token and how long it grants. The reservation is inert: the client leaving without
committing it discards it, so a relaunch abandoned at this point changes nothing.

hold_ms.description:
How long, once this client has left, its replacement may take to claim the slot. The
server grants up to its own limit and says what it granted; zero asks for its default.

oneOf.description:
Commit the reservation `token` names; answered by [`ServerMessage::HandoffCommitted`]. A
committed reservation is ready, but still holds nothing: a connection lost now is an
ordinary departure. Only [`Self::DepartForHandoff`] makes this client's departure hold its
slot.

The last thing a client being replaced says before its connection ends: hold the slot
`token` reserves, committed, for the replacement. From then on the client is in transit
until an attach presents the token or the reservation expires: the layout-control lease is
not handed on, and an ephemeral session does not count the gap as having no client. Not
answered: the client has already let go. One that never arrives leaves an ordinary
departure, and the replacement attaches without the held place.

Discard the reservation `token` names, whichever connection made it: the relaunch it was for
failed and the client stays. The token is the authority, so a client that had to reconnect
can still take back what it reserved. Answered by [`ServerMessage::HandoffAborted`] once no
reservation for the token remains.
Heartbeat reply to a [`ServerMessage::Ping`].

Pane input that also asks for [`ServerMessage::InputMarked`] with the same `token`.

The server writes the bytes and queues the answer in one step, before it looks at the pane's
output again. Everything the pane forwarded before the answer was produced before this input
reached it, and everything after may be the input's own response - which is how a UI tells a
program's answer from what was already on screen. A separate mark frame could not say this:
the server may drain the answer to the input between reading the two.

Drag-and-drop escape codes (OSC 72) for a pane's program, from the client running the drag
over it. Sending them makes this client the one the pane's answers go to, as
[`ServerMessage::PaneDragAndDrop`], until the drag is over.
Upload a regular file and paste its server-side path into a fixed pane generation.

List one directory **on the server's host** for the sidebar file tree.

Answered by [`ServerMessage::DirectoryListing`].

show_hidden.description: Include dotfiles. Mirrors `[sidebar] tree.show_hidden` on the client.

oneOf.description:
Scan a repository **on the server's host** for changed paths.

Answered by [`ServerMessage::ChangeListing`]. Backs the file tree's `Changes` projection,
which cannot use local git discovery when the files live on another machine.
Run Git worktree operations on this session server's host.
Ask for an immediate server-owned resource sample.
Delete the session: end its panes and discard its snapshot and deployments.

End the session's panes and discard its snapshot, leaving its deployments for whatever
starts under this name next.

Any `type` this build does not know: a request from a newer peer that skipped the send gate.

Decoded so the connection survives, answered with
[`super::UNSUPPORTED_MESSAGE_ERROR_CODE`], and never sent.

ClientResyncMetrics.description: Clients that fell too far behind to take a pane's output, had it shed, and caught up by replay.

exports.description:
Pane screens exported for resyncs. A pane that falls behind again mid-resync is exported
again by a later resync, so this tracks `started` under a flood.

last_export_us.description:
Time the server loop spent exporting one pane screen for any replay. Every client waits on
this, which is what a slow client's resyncs can cost a healthy one.

requeued_panes.description:
Panes put back in a replay queue because the client fell behind them again before their
replay finished, during an attach or a resync.

shed_bytes.description: Encoded pane output dropped instead of delivered, across this server process's lifetime.

ControlErrorCode.description:
Machine-readable control failure categories.

Human text may gain context or be reworded. These kebab-case values are the contract scripts
should branch on.

ControlLayoutKind.description: A tiling algorithm, as `layout get` names it.

oneOf.description: Verified caller identity on a server; attachment metadata on a UI.
List the panes this endpoint can see.
The panes of every session this UI has attached, on screen or not.

Report workspaces and where each pane sits. `workspace` is one-based and narrows the report
to that workspace.
Set a workspace's tiling algorithm, its master share, or both. `workspace` is one-based.

if_revision.description: Refuse with `conflict` unless the layout is still at this revision.

master_ratio.description: The master pane's share of a Master workspace, from 0.2 to 0.8.

oneOf.description:
Set one pane's floating, fullscreen, and floating-rect state. Omitted fields are left as
they are; a request that changes nothing succeeds with `changed: false`.

rect.description: Floating rect in canonical-canvas cells. Mutually exclusive with `rect_fraction`.

rect_fraction.description: Floating rect as fractions of the canonical canvas.

split_ratio.description: The pane's share of the Dwindle split directly holding it, from 0.2 to 0.8.

width_ratio.description: The pane's Scrollable column width as a fraction of the viewport, from 0.2 to 0.8.

oneOf.description: Move a pane to another workspace, at the end of its tiling order. `workspace` is one-based.
Exchange the places of two tiled panes in one workspace.

Scroll a Scrollable strip so a pane is in view, without moving focus. The viewport is
client-local, so only a UI answers; the shared layout and its revision do not change.

Close a pane, ending its process. The request is the confirmation; `[confirm]` does not
apply.
List the agents detected in panes.

Every agent this UI knows about: the session on screen, its other local sessions, and every
connected host, the ones that want attention first. Reached through `agents list --all`.

Go to an agent wherever it runs: focus its pane in the session on screen, or switch to or
attach its session first. Takes a `location` from `agents-overview`.
Read one agent's record.
Capture the text of an agent's pane.
Report runtime metrics.

Report this client's extension runtimes and the placed extension processes running through
them: where each runs, under which generation and bundle, and why one that is not running
is unavailable.

Upload a chunk of an extension bundle to a session server. `offset` is the byte in the
canonical archive this chunk starts at; `last` finishes the upload and verifies it. A chunk
that does not continue where the stored upload ended is refused rather than guessed at.

data.description: Base64 of the archive bytes in this chunk.

id.description:
The extension ID the bundle must declare. Named `id`, not `extension`, because that name
belongs to the caller's provenance on the request around this command.

oneOf.description:
Forget a session's deployment of one extension. The files stay if another deployment uses
the same digest.

id.description: The extension ID to forget; see [`Self::ExtensionsDeploy`] for why it is not `extension`.

oneOf.description:
List the extensions a session server holds, with the digest and generation each was
deployed under and whether its files still verify.
Move this client's focus to a pane.

Send literal text to a pane. `wait` holds the reply until the pane answers; see
[`PaneWait`].

capture.description: Return the pane's screen in this render once `wait` resolves. Needs `wait`.

scale.description: Enlarges a `png` capture, from 1 (the default) to 3.

oneOf.description:
Send named keys and/or literal text chunks to a pane (tmux-style key names). `wait`,
`capture`, and `scale` mean what they do for `send-text`.

literal.description: When true, every entry in `keys` is forwarded as literal UTF-8 (no key-name parsing).

oneOf.description: Open a pane.

argv.description: Direct executable and arguments. Mutually exclusive with `command`.

command.description: Shell command line interpreted by the configured command runner.

focus.description:
Move focus (and the active workspace) to the new pane. Defaults to `false`: the control
endpoint is an automation surface, and a pane spawned by an agent must not pull the
cursor out from under whoever is typing. Overrides a matched `[[rules]]` `focus`; the
rule still decides workspace, float, and fullscreen.

local_cwd.description:
CLI-resolved directory on the caller's host. Used only for local spawns;
a UI attached to a remote session uses `cwd` on that host instead.

size.description:
The terminal size the pane starts at, instead of the size its tile will get.

What this is for: a pane no UI draws - one in a workspace nobody is looking at, or one a
detached session opened - never gets a tile to measure, so it keeps its spawn size. A
script that captures such a pane chooses that size here, including sizes no window
could show. Once a UI draws the pane, the tile decides its size as it does for any other.

split_ratio.description:
The new pane's share of the Dwindle split it opens, committed with the spawn: the same
share `pane-set` sets with `split_ratio`, and refused wherever that one is.

target.description:
The pane to split, as if it had focus, instead of the caller's or the focused pane. Its
workspace is the one the pane opens in, so it cannot go with `workspace`. The split's
direction still follows the tile's shape, and a layout that orders its panes rather
than splitting them adds the pane at the end, as it does for a person's split.

workspace.description:
One-based workspace to spawn into, instead of the caller's. Overrides a matched
`[[rules]]` workspace, which is a default for panes a person opens.

What this is for: a script that opens panes into the workspace someone is working in
re-tiles their layout on every spawn. Naming a workspace of its own keeps the spawn
entirely out of the way, and gives each pane the same geometry as the last.

oneOf.description: Run any keybindable `Action` by its stable id (see `Action::id`/`Action::from_id`).
Call a deployed action with JSON arguments and answer with its JSON result.

timeout_ms.description: Shortens the action's own deadline. It can never lengthen it.

oneOf.description: The action calls running in this session.
Stop a running action call. The call itself answers `invocation-cancelled`.
Every action deployed in this session, with its schemas.

Capture a pane. Without `scrollback`, returns the current visible snapshot grid.
With `scrollback`, returns scrollback history (`"full"` or a trailing line count).
`render` picks plain text, an ANSI-styled document, a PNG, or styled runs as JSON; the
styled forms capture the visible grid only. `scale` enlarges a PNG, from 1 (the default) to
3. `image_pixels` adds each image's pixels to a `spans` capture. `wait` holds the capture
until the visible screen shows some text or stops changing; see [`PaneWait`].

Capture the whole client as it is drawn: the bar, borders, overlays, and every visible
pane. Answered from the next frame the UI paints, so it needs a UI; a session server
draws nothing.

image_pixels.description: Adds each image's pixels to a `spans` capture.

scale.description: Enlarges a PNG, from 1 (the default) to 3.

oneOf.description: Switch the active workspace. `index` is 1-based (1-9), matching the on-screen tabs.
Move the focused pane to another workspace. `index` is 1-based (1-9).
Open a command in this client's popup pane.

keep_open.description:
Hold the popup open after the command exits, matching the `[keys]` `popup` default; set
`false` for a program that owns the popup for its whole life.

oneOf.description:
Publish the logical agents or activities running inside the calling pane, and receive
activations for them. Unlike every other command this connection stays open in both
directions; closing it withdraws this publisher's rows. Reached through `rozi publish`.

kind.description:
What the publisher is: `activity` (the default) or `agent`. Only an agent publisher's
rows are agents.

name.description:
Distinguishes several publishers of one caller in the same pane; see
[`crate::state::PublisherIdentity`].

oneOf.description:
Publish rows into a sidebar stream tab and receive activations, expansions, actions, and
visibility for them. Like `publish`, the connection stays open both ways, and closing it
withdraws this producer's rows. Reached through `rozi sidebar publish`.

name.description: Distinguishes several producers of one caller in the same place.

tab.description:
The tab: an extension names its own tab's local name, anything else a `config.toml`
stream tab's id.

oneOf.description: Stream events as line-delimited JSON until the endpoint closes.
Turn logging of a pane's output on or off.
Set or clear a pane's reported status.
Wait for an agent to reach a condition.
Type a prompt into an agent, optionally waiting for it to reach a condition.
Read the latest response for one exact agent incarnation.
Report an agent's state from its own integration, for a pane.

ended.description:
With `unless_quiet`: the agent has confirmed the turn ended, so a report no screen
speaks for falls to that state instead of holding `working`.

unless_quiet.description:
With `working`: the state to fall to once the screen shows the agent has stopped, for
a reporter that cannot know a later report will follow. `reason` describes that state.

oneOf.description: Withdraw an integration's agent report from a pane.

Raise a toast from a script.

The automation surface can act but not report: a command that closes its own picker, or
runs under `[keys] exec` with no pane, finishes invisibly. This is the "useful off-screen
result" toasts are reserved for - not a receipt for something already on screen.

Show or hide one of the calling extension's own commands in the command palette.

Only an extension process may send it, for a command its own manifest declares. The choice
lasts as long as the extension's runtime generation, even after the calling command exits.
A process-facing change rotates the generation and restarts its services, resetting the
choice to the manifest's `hidden`. A presentation-only or no-op reload keeps both the
generation and the choice. A hidden command still runs from its key binding and
`run-action`: the palette lists what is worth
offering now, and the extension knows that better than the manifest can.

command.description: The command's ID: its manifest `id`, or the public `<extension>.<id>`.

oneOf.description:
Start recording a pane's screen to a file on the session server's host. Served by a session
server, which records the pane's canonical screen with or without a UI; a UI forwards it.
Every change is written, at most `max_fps` times a second, until `record-stop`, the pane
exiting, the session ending, or a limit. `follow` holds the reply until the recording ends
and stops it when the request's connection closes. Limits left out come from the server's
`[recording]` config.

force.description: Replace an existing regular file at `output`.

output.description:
An absolute path. The CLI resolves a relative one against its working directory. Left
out, the server names a new file in `[recording] dir`.

oneOf.description:
Stop recordings and answer once every file is complete: recording `id`, or every recording
of pane `target`, or, with neither, the only recording running.
List the recordings running in the session.

Add a labelled mark to recording `id`, or to every recording of pane `target`, or, with
neither, to every running recording.

Start recording the UI that serves the request: every frame it paints, chrome included, at
most `max_fps` times a second, into a file on the UI's host, until `record-ui-stop`, the UI
exiting, or a limit. Served by a UI only; limits left out come from its `[recording]`
config.

force.description: Replace an existing regular file at `output`.

hide_indicator.description:
Leave the `REC` chip off the screen while this recording runs, and so out of it. Off,
`[recording] ui_indicator` decides.

output.description:
An absolute path. The CLI resolves a relative one against its working directory. Left
out, the UI names a new file in `[recording] dir`.

oneOf.description: Stop the UI's recording and answer once its file is complete.
Add a labelled mark to the UI's recording.
Show a picker in this client and stream the selection back.

actions.description: Extra chords offered beside select and cancel, advertised in the footer.

empty.description: Copy shown when the row list is empty and the filter is empty.

tab.description: Id of the tab to open on. Omitted or unknown opens the first.

tabs.description:
Pages shown as a tab strip, each with its own rows, filter, and highlight. Omitted is
one untitled page and no strip.

width.description: Modal width in columns, clamped to a readable range. Omitted uses the shared default.

oneOf.description: Ask for one line of text in a modal prompt, with no picker behind it.

masked.description: Hide typed characters on screen. The submitted `input` is still plaintext on the stream.

caller_context.description:
Verified caller session and pane generation. A UI must still display this session when it
executes the command; the session server also checks the pane generation.

credential.description:
The worker credential of a placed extension process, from `ROZI_EXTENSION_CREDENTIAL`.
Automatically attached by the CLI. When present, the UI identifies the caller from it alone
and replaces `extension` with what the credential was issued for.

extension.description: Automatically attached by the CLI when launched from an extension process.

source_session.description:
The session server `source_pane` belongs to, from the caller's `ROZI_SESSION_INSTANCE`.
Absent when the caller is not a shared pane of a session.

ControlResponse.description:
The answer to one control request, in the `{ok, data, error}` shape every control surface
speaks.

`Deserialize` because this crosses the session wire as well as the UI endpoint: a headless
[`ClientMessage::SessionControl`](crate::session::protocol::ClientMessage::SessionControl)
reply carries one of these, and the CLI reads it back as the same type the UI produced.

code.description:
Stable failure category for scripts. Absent on successful replies and on replies from
older Rozi versions.

ControllerChangeReason.description: Why the layout-control lease moved. Carried by [`ServerMessage::ControllerChanged`].

oneOf.description: The controller detached or dropped cleanly.
The controller missed heartbeats and was disconnected.

The lease was granted: the first attacher, promotion of the oldest survivor, a controller's
explicit grant, or an auto-grant to a requester when no controller held the lease.
A value from a newer peer this build does not know. Never sent.

agent.description:
Shared rather than owned: one definition's identity describes every pane running that
agent, and this rides inside [`PaneRuntimeState`], which is recomputed per pane at the
runtime poll rate and sits in the largest `Msg`/`ServerMessage` variants. Two inline
`String`s here cost 48 bytes in each of them and an allocation per sweep.

oneOf.description:
`rozi record stop`, the foreground `rozi record pane` exiting, or the UI's Stop recording
command.
It reached its `--duration`.
It reached its `--max-bytes`.
The pane's program exited.
The pane was closed or replaced.
The session was killed.
The session server shut down.
Writing the file failed, such as on a full disk. The file holds what was written before.
The recorded UI exited.

ExtensionProvenance.description:
Provenance carried automatically by the CLI for a process launched by an extension.

The opaque generation is a fencing token, not authentication: it rejects processes from a
retired runtime definition, but another process running as the same user is inside Rozi's trust
boundary and may be able to observe it.

FractionRect.description:
A rectangle as fractions of the canonical canvas, so `0.5` is half its width or height.
Fractions outside `0.0..=1.0` mean the same thing as an out-of-canvas [`CellRect`].

GraphicsSessionMetrics.description: Semantic graphics supersession is counted separately from overload/resync loss.

LayoutReport.description:
What `layout get` answers with.

Two views of one arrangement, kept apart because they are different facts. The workspaces and
each pane's `rect` describe the session's shared layout document, which the server owns and
every client reconciles to: the same answer whichever endpoint is asked. `client`, and each
pane's `view_rect`, describe what one UI actually draws, which depends on its own viewport,
chrome, and focus, and so exists only when a UI answered.

A public document rather than the internal `SharedLayout` itself: that one is a synchronization
format versioned with the session protocol, and this is the contract scripts read.

canvas.description:
The canonical canvas every `rect` is measured against, in cells. It is the canvas of the
client that last controlled the layout. Absent with `revision`.

client.description: This UI's own view of the layout. Absent from a session endpoint, which has no screen.

revision.description:
Layout revision this report describes. Absent while no layout document exists, which is the
case for a session whose panes nothing has placed yet.

session.description: Session that answered, qualified with its host when remote.

unplaced_panes.description:
Panes the session runs that no layout document places yet. Only a session endpoint reports
these; a UI places every pane it knows about.

PaletteAction.description: An action a client may offer in its palette: it needs no arguments.

PaneBorderMode.description:
Structural presentation of pane borders. Glyph shape remains independently controlled by
`PaneBorderStyle`; this mode decides whether pane frames or internal split dividers are drawn.

PaneCommandPhase.description:
Mirrors [`TerminalCommandPhase`] on the wire (that framework type has no `serde` impls, since
it is UI-agnostic runtime state rather than persisted/transmitted data).

oneOf.description: Also what a phase from a newer peer decodes as.

PaneCwdSource.description:
Which precedence tier produced [`PaneRuntimeState::cwd`].

Tier order, most to least authoritative: a remote [`ShellReport`](Self::ShellReport), then the
directory a program the shell is running was started in
([`ProcessInspector`](Self::ProcessInspector)), then a
local `OSC 7`/`OSC 9;9` [`ShellReport`](Self::ShellReport), then the shell's own directory
([`ProcessInspector`](Self::ProcessInspector), native `/proc` or `libproc` inspection) ->
[`LaunchDirectory`](Self::LaunchDirectory) (the directory the pane was
spawned with). A configured-fallback fourth tier from the plan's precedence table collapses
into `LaunchDirectory` here: the launch cwd a pane starts with is already itself resolved from
config/profile defaults, so there is no separate value a fourth tier could contribute once
launch has happened.

oneOf.description: Also what a source from a newer peer decodes as.

PaneDragAndDrop.description: What a pane's program registered for drag and drop (OSC 72).

drags.description: Set while the program offers drags.

drops.description: Set while the program accepts drops.

client_id.description: The `i` key the program registered with.

machine_id.description: The protocol machine id of the host running the program.

client_id.description: The `i` key the program registered with.

machine_id.description: The protocol machine id of the host running the program.

mimes.description: Extra MIME types the program asked for.

PaneInfo.description:
One pane as `list-panes` reports it.

Both control surfaces fill this same type. A UI endpoint reads it out of the client's `State`
and a session server reads it out of its own authoritative runtime, but the document a script
parses is the contract, not either implementation - so there is one type describing it rather
than two that have to be kept in step by hand.

agent.description:
The agent detection recognized behind this pane, by definition id, and what it reads the
pane as doing. Both absent when no definition matched. This is detection's own answer, not
the pane's `reported_status` - a script capturing screens to test the rules against needs
to see what the rules currently say about the screen it just took.

agent_session.description:
The conversation the pane's own agent integration last reported through `agents report
--native-session`, while one owns the pane. A client that runs several conversations shows
this one; a publisher listing the others places each in the pane that shows it from this.

command.description: Initial launch intent, retained for automation and profile diagnostics.

foreground_pid.description:
Process group id of the running foreground job, while one runs and where the platform can
read it. A program that lists its own processes by pid matches them against this to find
the one in a pane. A UI endpoint omits it for a remote attachment, whose processes are on
another machine; a session endpoint answers for its own host.

foreground_program.description: Live foreground process: what the pane is running now, rather than what launched it.

on_screen.description:
Whether this pane's session is the one on screen. Pane ids repeat across sessions, so a
command naming a pane by id reaches this pane only while this is true.

recording.description: The session server is recording this pane; `record list` says where.

reference.description: Absent only from a UI endpoint that has no session behind it.

session.description:
Session that answered. A remote one is qualified with its host, so two same-name sessions
do not look interchangeable.

status.description:
Lifecycle text in the vocabulary a client's terminal reports: `ready`, or `exited (N)` for
a pane whose process is gone but whose screen is still readable.

workspace.description:
One-based workspace, or `0` when the session has no layout document yet - nothing has
placed the pane, so there is no workspace to name.

PaneLaunch.description:
How a pane's initial child process is launched.

Shell commands are intentionally distinct from direct argv. Direct execution never joins or
quotes its arguments into a command line, so spaces, Unicode, and shell metacharacters retain
their literal process-argument meaning on every platform.

fullscreen.description:
A fullscreen pane covers the whole screen while it is fullscreen; `rect` stays the place it
returns to.

order.description:
Position in the workspace's tiling order, from `0`. This is the order Master, Grid, Columns,
Rows, Scrollable, and Monocle lay panes out in; absent for a floating pane.

pinned.description:
A pinned pane is floating and moves with the controlling client to every workspace it
switches to.

rect.description:
Placement on the canonical canvas, in cells, without gaps, borders, or the workbar - those
are each client's own presentation. Every pane in Monocle shares one rect.

rect_fraction.description: `rect` as fractions of the canonical canvas.

reference.description: Exact pane incarnation. Absent only from a UI with no session behind it.

split_ratio.description:
The pane's share of the Dwindle split directly holding it. Present only for a tiled pane
that shares a split in a Dwindle workspace.

view_rect.description:
Where the answering UI draws the pane, in its own terminal's cells, including gaps and
chrome. Present only for panes in the UI's active workspace.

width_ratio.description:
The pane's column width as a fraction of the viewport. Present only for a tiled pane in a
Scrollable workspace.

original_user.description:
Account that owns the session server and launched the pane's original shell. Additive and
optional so protocol-12/13 peers that predate this field remain compatible.

runtime.description:
Authoritative pane runtime state: CWD, command lifecycle,
and foreground executable, as tracked server-side from shell-integration OSC reports and
native process-inspection fallbacks. Present in every `Attached`/`SpawnResult`-adjacent
pane listing so a freshly attached client starts with current state rather than waiting for
the next [`super::ServerMessage::PaneRuntimeChanged`].

scrollback.description: Retained history capacity selected when the server created this pane.

PaneRef.description: Exact identity of one PTY incarnation.

PaneRuntimeState.description:
Authoritative pane runtime state: the server-owned `TerminalPty`/
`TerminalScreen` pair is the source of truth for all of this, combining shell-integration OSC
reports with native process-inspection fallbacks per [`PaneCwdSource`]'s precedence order.

`cwd` is always the *best available displayable* path regardless of source; `cwd_host` is set
only when that path names a location on a different host than the **session server** (a remote
`OSC 7` report over SSH into the server's machine, for instance). Under `--remote`, the server
still owns this comparison — paths on the remote session host have `cwd_host = None` even though
they are not on the client's machine. Client-local filesystem consumers (file tree, profile
save of paths) must therefore also check whether the client is remote-attached before treating
a `cwd_host`-free path as local. Spawn requests sent to the session server may still carry the
server-relative cwd.

agent_launch.description:
Which launch of the pane's screen-detected agent [`Self::detected_agent`] describes, counted
per pane. A new agent process - a supervisor restarting one under the same name, say - is a
new lifecycle rather than a state change, so a client compares this before reading an edge:
a run that died with its process did not finish, and the restart's loading screen reading
idle must not say it did.

display_path.description:
Server-computed compact cwd for pane chrome: project-qualified when inside a detected Git
project, otherwise home-relative or absolute. Optional for compatibility with older peers.

drag_and_drop.description:
What the pane's program registered for drag and drop (OSC 72), so a client knows where a
drag goes before it reaches the pane.

foreground_arguments.description:
Arguments [`Self::foreground_program`] was launched with, `argv[0]` excluded.

A name says which program a pane is running; only the arguments say what it is doing with
it, which is why a captured profile replays them - `claude` and `claude
--dangerously-skip-permissions` are the same executable and different panes. Empty while the
pane sits at a prompt with nothing running, when the platform cannot read another process's
arguments (macOS, Windows), when the inspected process is not the program the pane reports
running, or when an argument could not survive being typed back at a prompt.

foreground_executable.description:
Absolute path of the foreground executable, set **only** when [`Self::foreground_program`]
does not resolve on the session server's own `PATH`.

A pane started through a shell alias, a `./target` binary, or anything else off `PATH`
reports a name that no later launch could run, so a client replaying that program (profile
capture) launches this path instead. `None` is the ordinary case and means "the name is
enough" - or that the platform cannot read the path, which is every Windows pane.

Like [`Self::foreground_arguments`], this describes a command that is running *now*: a pane
at its prompt reports neither, even though [`Self::foreground_program`] still names the
last command it ran.

foreground_pid.description:
Process group id of the job running in the foreground, on the session server's host:
its leader's pid. Set only while a command runs and where the platform can read it.

The group, not each member, because a running program spawns and reaps children
constantly while its group stays put. This is what lets a program that enumerates its own
processes tell which of them is the one in this pane.

foreground_program.description:
Reconciled logical foreground identity as a normalized executable basename, never a path or
command line. Shell intent is retained for interpreted commands; native evidence replaces a
shell alias or function when the platform can prove which executable took over.

foreground_programs.description:
Basename-only identities observed across the PTY's current foreground process group.

POSIX terminals arbitrate input at process-group granularity, so there is no universally
correct single "input process" for pipelines or wrappers. Split-aware input routing checks
this complete, sampled set and falls back to [`Self::foreground_program`] when native
process inspection is unavailable (notably on Windows).

foreground_shell.description:
Whether [`Self::foreground_program`] is a shell rather than a program a shell runs: the
pane's own launch shell or a common shell name. Judged by the session server, on the host
that runs the pane - a client's shell configuration says nothing about another machine's.

git_branch.description:
Checked-out branch of `project_root`, or a short commit id when `HEAD` is detached. Read
from `HEAD` on a slow tick rather than derived from `cwd`, since a checkout changes it
without the directory moving.

last_exit_status.description:
The most recently observed exit status, from either an `OSC 133;D` report or the PTY child
itself exiting. Sticky across the next command's `Prompt`/`Input` phases so callers can
still show "last command exited N" at a fresh prompt.

project_root.description:
Absolute path of the Git project containing `cwd`, as the session server sees it. Set only
for a server-local `cwd` — a `cwd_host` path names a filesystem the server cannot probe.
This, not `cwd`, is what the sidebar groups agents by, so a pane in `repo/src` lands in the
same project as one in `repo`.

recording.description:
Whether the session server is recording this pane with `rozi record`. Clients mark the pane
for as long as it is, so a recording is never invisible.

repository.description:
Primary checkout when `project_root` is a linked Git worktree of it. A worktree is its own
project, but named after its directory (`.claude/worktrees/fix-login`) it reads as an
unrelated one; this is what lets it be labelled with the repository it belongs to.

rows.description:
Logical agents or activities this pane's program published for itself; empty for a pane that
publishes nothing - which is nearly all of them, and the path that stays unchanged.

A pane is one PTY but need not be one agent. A client with its own tab bar runs several
sessions behind one terminal and can only ever *draw* the one in view, so screen detection
sees a single state for several runs and cannot tell which of them it belongs to. A program
that knows all of them reports them here instead, and the server stops scraping that pane.

sequence.description:
Monotonic per-pane counter, bumped only when some other field in this struct actually
changed. [`super::ServerMessage::PaneRuntimeChanged`] carries this so a client that received
updates out of order (should not happen on a single ordered connection, but is cheap
insurance) can detect and ignore a stale one.

work_started_at.description:
Unix timestamp for the current active agent run. It is retained while an agent is blocked
or reports another non-quiescent status, so clients can show one continuous run age after a
block/resume transition and after detach/reattach.

PaneSize.description: A terminal size in cells, as `split --size COLSxROWS` spells it.

PaneTitlebarMode.description:
Structural presentation of a visible pane title. `Bar` is the existing separate title row above
the frame; `Border` and `Integrated` reuse the frame's top border row; `Inset` writes the title
inside the frame, on the first interior row beneath the top border. Visibility is controlled
independently by `pane.show_titles`, so toggling it never loses the selected layout.

PaneWait.description:
Hold a `capture-pane`, `send-text`, or `send-keys` reply until the pane's visible screen shows
`text`, stops changing for `settle_ms`, or both, in that order.

Both conditions read the screen as it is drawn - its grid of cells - rather than the bytes the
program wrote. A redraw that paints the same cells again, a cursor that only moves, and a title
change are not changes, which is what "the screen settled" has to mean for a program that
repaints on a timer.

`text` is a literal substring of one visible row, matched against the untrimmed row. For
`capture-pane` it matches whatever is on screen, including text that was already there. For
`send-text` and `send-keys` it matches only rows the input's answer produced: text on screen
when the input was written does not count, even after it scrolls.

A wait that outlives `timeout_ms` fails with `timeout`; a pane whose program exits, or that
closes, fails with `pane-not-running`. Both carry the pane's capture in `data` when the pane is
still there to capture.

settle_ms.description:
How long the visible screen must stay unchanged, in milliseconds. With `text`, the clock
starts once the text has appeared.

text.description: Literal text to wait for on one visible row. Must be non-empty, with no line break.

timeout_ms.description: Deadline for the whole wait, in milliseconds, at most [`MAX_PANE_WAIT_MS`].

PickAction.description:
One extra key the caller offers alongside select and cancel.

Actions are what turn a picker from a menu into a working surface: delete the branch under the
cursor and push a fresh list, or open a prompt and create one. They are declared up front so the
footer can advertise them the way every built-in picker advertises its own chords.

close.description:
Whether firing it ends the picker. Default `false`: the caller usually wants to push an
updated row set and keep going.

confirm.description:
Require a second press to fire, the way the session and profile pickers arm a kill or a
delete. The armed row is struck through in the error colour with an `again to <label>` cue,
and moving the highlight disarms it.

key.description: Chord that fires it, in the same spelling `[keys]` uses (`ctrl-n`).

prompt.description:
When set, the key opens a text prompt and the entered text rides back as `input`.
A string is the title. An object may also set placeholder, a seed value, and masking.
Cancelling the prompt returns to the picker without reporting anything.

from_query.description:
Seed the prompt with the picker's filter text, the way the session picker's `new` starts
from what was typed. `value` still applies while the filter is empty.

masked.description: Hide typed characters on screen. The submitted `input` is still plaintext on the stream.

PickPromptSpec.description:
How a pick action describes the stacked text prompt.

The string form is the title. The object form is additive: every existing `"prompt":"Title"`
caller stays valid.

PickTab.description: One tab a `pick` caller declares up front. Rows arrive per tab afterwards.

id.description:
Names the tab in row snapshots, and rides back as `tab` on selections, actions, and tab
switches. Row ids only need to be unique within their tab.

ProjectRowRef.description: A published row, by the pane that publishes it.

ProjectSummary.description: One checkout a session works in.

branch.description: Branch checked out at `root`, or a short commit id when `HEAD` is detached.

panes.description: Live panes whose working directory is inside this checkout.

repository.description:
The primary checkout `root` is a linked worktree of. Absent when `root` is the primary
checkout itself. Together with the host, this is what identifies a project across its
worktrees.

root.description: The checkout's root on the session's host: the primary checkout, or a linked worktree.

rows.description:
Published rows working in this checkout from a pane whose own directory is elsewhere — a
program running each of its agents in its own worktree.

PublishedAgentResponse.description: One response for a row owned by an open agent publisher. Sent beside, never inside, rows.

PublishedRow.description: One logical agent or activity inside a pane that publishes several.

active.description:
The row the publisher is currently displaying; at most one is true.

This is what lets a finish on a *background* row raise an alert even while the pane is
focused - looking at the pane only ever acknowledges the row on screen.

cwd.description:
Absolute directory this row's work happens in, on the pane's host. A program running
several sessions behind one terminal often runs each in its own Git worktree, so the pane's
own cwd says nothing about where any one of them is. Absent means the pane's cwd.

id.description:
Publisher-chosen identity, opaque to rozi and stable across updates. Unique only within
its publisher; see [`RowKey`].

Never a position: tabs are reordered and closed, and an index-keyed run clock would hand
one tab's elapsed time to whichever tab slid into its place.

kind.description:
Server-owned copy of the kind the publisher declared when its stream opened. Whatever a
publisher sends here is overwritten.

live_session.description:
The session id the process running this row reports its hooks under, when that is not
[`Self::native_session`].

A conversation can move to another process under a new id while it is still resumed by its
first one, as Claude Code does when it sends a conversation to the background. Hook reports
then name the new id, and only a report naming it speaks for the row; the first process's
last report no longer does.

native_session.description:
The agent's own conversation id for this row, when the row is one: what `--resume` takes.

It ties the row to the pane's [`AgentIntegrationReport`]: the hook-driven report speaks
for the row whose native session it names, unless the row names a
[`Self::live_session`] instead, so several conversations behind one client
stay listed while the one the hooks follow keeps their fresher state. It is also what
resurrection resumes when this row is the active one.

project.description: Server-owned project of [`Self::cwd`]. Whatever a publisher sends here is overwritten.

publisher.description:
Server-owned identity of the stream that published this row. Whatever a publisher sends
here is overwritten.

reported.description:
Whether a hook report, rather than the publisher, set this row's status and reason.
Server-owned: whatever a publisher sends here is overwritten.

status.description: Same vocabulary and same sanitization as [`PaneStatus::value`].

work_started_at.description:
Server-owned run start, mirroring [`PaneRuntimeState::work_started_at`] per row. Whatever
a publisher sends here is overwritten.

PublisherKind.description:
What a publisher declares itself to be when its stream opens.

An activity is something happening; an agent is something doing work. Every published row
appears in Activity, but only an agent publisher's rows are agents: listed by `rozi agents`,
targetable by `agents prompt`, counted by `keep_awake_while_agents_work`, and authoritative over
the pane's screen detection. Declared, never inferred from what detection happens to see.

QuietFallback.description:
What a report's `working` becomes if the screen shows the agent has stopped. See
[`AgentIntegrationReport::unless_quiet`].

ended.description:
The agent has confirmed the turn ended. Without it the fallback is only provisional, so
with no screen to read the report holds `working` until a confirmation arrives.

RecordingMetrics.description: Pane recordings on a session server.

dropped.description: Changes coalesced away because a writer fell behind, across running and finished recordings.

frames.description: Frames and bytes written, across running and finished recordings.

started.description: Recordings this server has started and finished.

RecordingStopped.description: A finished recording, as `record-stop` and a followed `record-start` report it.

dropped.description:
Changes the recorder never wrote because it had fallen behind and kept only the newest
state. Zero unless the disk could not keep up.

error.description: Why writing failed, for a `write-failed` reason.

RemoteDrag.description:
Another client's tiled drag, mirrored here so every attached client lifts the same pane out of
the same tiling.

This is presence state, not layout: it rides its own wire messages instead of
[`SharedLayout`](crate::layout::shared::SharedLayout), because a half-lifted pane must never be
persisted, resurrected, or inherited by whoever takes the control lease next. It is cleared
whenever the controller changes, so a disconnect mid-gesture heals into the authoritative
layout rather than leaving a pane floating forever.

Only *tiled* drags need it. A floating pane's rectangle is already part of the shared document,
so dragging one replicates through the ordinary layout commit.

rect.description:
The lifted rectangle, as fractions of the controller's canonical canvas - the same frame
[`SharedPane::rect`](crate::layout::shared::SharedPane::rect) uses, so a follower with a
different viewport letterboxes it exactly like a floating pane.

last_blocking_us.description:
The part of an attempt the server loop itself is blocked for: capturing pane replay bytes
and metadata, before the durable write is handed to the snapshot worker. This is the figure
that bounds input latency during a snapshot; `last_duration_us` no longer does.

last_duration_us.description:
Complete attempt duration: the server-thread export plus the worker's write, sync, and
rename. Comparable with the synchronous measurements recorded before snapshots moved off
the server loop.

last_exported_panes.description:
How the last capture split between re-exporting changed panes and reusing the replay files
unchanged ones already had. A snapshot that blocks for a long time is explained by these:
cost tracks exported panes and their bytes, not the session's pane count.

RowKey.description:
A published row's identity within its pane: the publisher that owns it and the id it chose.

Row ids are the publisher's own, so two publishers in one pane may pick the same one. Everything
keyed by a row - run clocks, finish edges, activation, agent slots - keys by this pair.

RowProject.description: The Git project a published row's `cwd` lies in, as the session server resolved it.

branch.description: Branch checked out at `root`, or a short commit id when `HEAD` is detached.

repository.description: Primary checkout `root` is a linked worktree of; see [`PaneRuntimeState::repository`].

root.description: Project root containing the row's `cwd`: a linked worktree's own root, not its repository.

SerializedTree.description: Serde-stable tree shared by profile TOML and the session layout document.

oneOf.description: Sent before a new pane's layout or output, including to the spawning client.
Acknowledges one upload step. The final acknowledgement follows path insertion.
A peer's release and the session wire generations it speaks.

effective_protocol.description: Negotiated wire generation for this connection.

handoff_claimed.description:
Whether the attach's `handoff_token` claimed a reserved slot. Present only when the
attach presented one.

protocol_min.description:
Server's minimum supported protocol version, so a client can tell whether another build
could attach to this same server. Absent from a server that predates it.

rozi_version.description: The server's release (`CARGO_PKG_VERSION`), so a client can name what a session runs.

oneOf.description: Retained inbox delivered immediately after attach, before live notification events.
The deployed actions a client can offer in its palette, sent on attach and when they change.
Reply to a [`ClientMessage::Query`] probe.

effective_protocol.description: Negotiated wire generation for this probe.

instance.description:
The answering server's [`super::SessionInstanceId`]. A pane finds its own server by it
when it has no UI to ask: a session name can be reused or renamed, an instance cannot.
Missing on servers that predate it, which a caller must treat as "not mine".

oneOf.description:
Reply to a [`ClientMessage::SessionControl`] request.

The payload is the same `{ok, data, error}` document the UI control endpoint returns, so a
script reads one response shape whether it reached a running UI or a detached session.

effective_protocol.description: Negotiated wire generation for this request.

oneOf.description: Acknowledges an integration report sent over an attached client connection.
Reply to a [`ClientMessage::AttachedControl`] request, carrying its `request_id`.

cell_width.description:
The pane's cell size in pixels, as its controller reported it. Every client parses the
pane against it, so an image covers the same cells for a follower whose own cells
differ. Zero when no client has reported one.

oneOf.description:
Discard this client's parsed screen for a shared pane and start a fresh one at the given
geometry. The pane's replay follows, so the client ends up where the server's screen was
when it exported. Sent before every replay: on attach, and when a client that fell behind
had the pane's live output shed.

cell_width.description: The pane's cell size in pixels. See [`ServerMessage::Resized`]'s `cell_width`.

oneOf.description:
Drag-and-drop escape codes (OSC 72) a pane's program wrote, for the client that owns the
pane's drag: the last one to send [`ClientMessage::DragAndDrop`] to it.

Authoritative terminal program records. Revision and generation fence stale snapshots;
attach baselines initialize presentation without replaying historical alerts.

initial.description: Initial attach baseline, applied without attention or historical notifications.

snapshot.description: A framework type, opaque to the schema; the golden wire corpus pins its JSON shape.

oneOf.description:
A pane's [`PaneRuntimeState`] changed: broadcast after raw
pane output for the same event, once the server has both processed the bytes into the
screen and re-derived runtime state from them. `generation` guards against a message that
raced a respawn; `state.sequence` guards against out-of-order delivery.

A new layout revision was accepted; broadcast to every client including its author (so the
author confirms its own rev from the echo and all clients see one identical rev sequence).

live.description:
The revision is one step of a gesture still under the controller's pointer, so a
follower draws it as is rather than easing toward it - easing toward every step would
leave the follower's panes trailing the pointer for the whole gesture.

oneOf.description:
A commit was rejected (stale base rev or non-controller). Sent to the committer only, with
the authoritative layout so the rejection self-heals.

The controller's in-flight tiled drag moved, or ended (`drag: None`).

Broadcast to every client including its author, like [`Self::LayoutCommitted`], so there is
one relay path rather than a special case; the author recognises `author` as itself and
keeps its own drag session. Nothing on the server survives this message - a client that
misses the trailing `None` clears the drag on the next
[`Self::ControllerChanged`] instead, which every disconnect and lease move already emits.

Sent only to the current controller when `from` requests the lease. Debounced per requester so
repeated requests cannot spam the controller; the sticky badge lives in the roster instead.
Sent only to a requester whose pending control request the controller declined.

Reply to [`ClientMessage::PrepareHandoff`]: the token that claims this client's slot, and how
long the slot is held once the client has gone, which may be less than was asked for.
`error` is set, and `token` empty, when the server refused.

Reply to [`ClientMessage::CommitHandoff`]. `error` is set when nothing was committed: the
token is unknown, spent, or expired.

Reply to [`ClientMessage::AbortHandoff`]: no reservation for that token remains, whether it
was just discarded or was already gone.
Answer to [`ClientMessage::MarkedInput`].

Reply to [`ClientMessage::ListDirectory`]. `error` is set instead of `entries` when the
server could not read the directory; the client renders it in the tree row.

Reply to [`ClientMessage::ListChanges`]. An empty list with no `error` means a clean tree or
a root that is not a repository.
Reply to [`ClientMessage::Worktree`], matched by request ID after asynchronous execution.
Server-owned resource sample, requested by a protocol-18 client.

A pane recording ended without being stopped: it reached a limit, writing failed, or its
pane exited or closed. Broadcast so a UI can say so; a stopped recording already answered
whoever stopped it.
Authoritative session event emitted by the session server.
Typed record streamed to a session subscriber.

Any `type` this build does not know: a message from a newer server that skipped the send
gate. Decoded so the connection survives, logged once, ignored, and never sent.

recordings.description: Pane recordings (`rozi record`). Absent from a server that predates them.

SessionEvent.description: One sequenced event recorded by a [`SessionServer`](super::SessionServer).

SessionInstanceId.description:
Opaque identity of one running session-server process.

Names can be reused and pane generations restart after a server dies. This non-persistent token
fences references from one server instance away from every later server with the same name.

SessionNotification.description: A notification retained by its session and presented independently by each client.

SessionSubscribeRecord.description: Typed records streamed by a session subscription.

oneOf.description: One sequenced event recorded by a [`SessionServer`](super::SessionServer).

The session stopped cleanly, so nothing more will come. A stream that closes without this or
[`Self::Lagged`] was cut short.

SessionSubscribeSnapshot.description: Current snapshot of a session as streamed at subscription start when `--snapshot` is requested.

SharedLayout.description:
The complete shared window-manager document for a session. Fractions in [`FracRect`] are
relative to the controller's canonical pane canvas (`canvas_cols` × `canvas_rows`, excluding
the workbar) so followers place floats inside the same centered canvas.

pinned.description: Carried to whichever workspace the controller switches to. Only a floating pane is pinned.

rect.description: Fractions of the canonical canvas; `Some` only for floating panes.

replay.description:
See [`crate::state::PaneIdentity::replay`]. Shared so a follower that takes control
respawns an exited profile pane through the interactive shell, not the command runner.
Defaulted so layout documents committed before this field existed still parse.

scrollable_width.description: Scrollable column width as a fraction of the tile viewport.

SharedPaneGeometry.description:
Geometry-affecting presentation shared with followers so their terminal grids match.
Colors, border glyphs, and animation recipes remain client-local.

SpawnPlacementCommit.description: An optimistic document publication committed atomically with a shared pane spawn.

path.description: Path relative to the scanned root.

WireChangeState.description: Serde-stable mirror of the framework's git change states.

oneOf.description: A value from a newer peer this build does not know. Never sent.

ignored.description: Whether the server's ignore rules exclude this entry.

name.description: Name relative to the listed directory, never a path.

symlink_target.description:
Where a symlink points, spelled the way the link itself spells it, so the tree can show
`link → target` for a file it cannot read from this side of the connection. `None` for
everything that is not a link, and for a link the server could not read.

master_ratio.description: The master pane's share of the width. Present only for a Master workspace.

panes.description: Tiled panes in tiling order, then floating panes.

synchronized.description: Whether typed input is broadcast to every pane in the workspace.

WorktreeLock.description: A checkout Git has locked against removal and pruning.

reason.description: Git's lock reason, empty when the lock gave none.

stale.description:
The reason names a process (`pid <N>`) that is no longer running on the repository's host.
A reason that names no process is never stale.

path.description: Absolute checkout path on the session server's host; remote clients keep it opaque.

oneOf.description: Read-only provider status, on a separate worker from checkout operations.

path.description: Absent for a server-generated sibling path. Remote clients never interpret this path.

delete_branch.description: Which copies of the checkout's branch to delete afterwards, when merged.

unlock_stale.description: Lift a lock whose owning process is gone first. The server checks that itself.

oneOf.description: Lift a linked checkout's Git lock.
Add a top-level directory of the repository to its `.git/info/exclude`.
A value from a newer peer this build does not know. Never sent.

sessions.description:
Sessions on the host that record each listed checkout (by its listed path) as their
origin. Checked on the host, so a client need not discover sessions to show them.

unignored.description: The repository's top-level directory this path would add, when Git does not ignore it.

branches.description: What became of each branch copy the request asked to delete.

oneOf.description: A value from a newer peer this build does not know. Never sent.

WorktreeSession.description: A session that records a checkout as its origin.

running.description: Its server is running. Otherwise it is a snapshot that can be restored.

WorktreeStatuses.description: Keyed by the host's checkout path. An error means status is unavailable, not that no PR exists.

description: Control frames exchanged between a rozi session server and its clients, CLI callers, and remote proxies. Generated; see dev/wire-compatibility.md for the rules every change to it follows.
